Our Story

Four decades on
Bliss Street

Faysal opened on Bliss Street beside the American University of Beirut, and has fed the neighbourhood ever since — students, taxi drivers, night-shift workers and families, at every hour of the day and night.

The menu grew into the sprawling list it is today: manakish, fatayer, arayes, sfiha, sambousek, the famous Special Faysal. But the dough is still rolled by hand, the za'atar still mixed in-house, and the cheese is still real.

"One of the oldest snacks in Beirut — where locals like me have eaten since kindergarten, until we had families of our own."

It doesn't look like much, and there's barely room to sit — it's a takeaway corner at heart, now with delivery 24/24. But the fatayer are crunchy, the manakish generous, and the smell reaches you down the street.

The Craft

Why locals keep coming back

Reviewers say it themselves — it's the real ingredients and the dough that set Faysal apart.

The Oven
A hot oven gives the dough its blistered crust — crisp underneath, tender within. One regular noted their man'oushe was still soft a day later, from the fridge.
The Dough
Rolled by hand, fresh daily — the detail locals point to again and again. No frozen shortcuts. There's even a brown wholewheat dough and a bran option.
Real Cheese
"They use real cheese for their mna2eesh — that makes a difference." Generously loaded, every item earns its price.
